source_name: MNB Fizetési rendszer jelentés (annual Payment Systems Report)
why_relevant: Annual analytical report on the operation of VIBER and the GIRO-operated BKR, including availability, incident, concentration and turnover analysis, plus commentary on AFR uptake. Interprets operator data the operator itself does not narrate publicly.

source_name: MNB – Módszertani útmutató a készpénzforgalmazásról (cash handling methodology guide)
why_relevant: Operational rulebook for cash recirculation, banknote authentication machine testing and reporting duties imposed on banks and cash processors — defines what compliance data CIT firms and ATM operators must generate.

source_name: MNB – Költségvetési jelentés (fiscal/budget analysis report series)
why_relevant: MNB's analysis of the annual budget act discusses planned and realised revenue lines, including transaction-levy receipts — an independent cross-check on Ministry of Finance figures and on implied payment turnover.

source_name: MNB Szemle / MNB-tanulmányok research on Hungarian cash demand and payment habits
why_relevant: MNB research output (e.g. analysis of the change in Hungarian cash demand; MT143 household payment habits 2020) explains the drivers behind the headline cash and card series — hoarding vs transactional demand, demographic split of card use.

source_name: MNB Occasional Paper 96 – A bankközi jutalék szerepe a kártyás fizetési rendszerekben / The role of the interchange fee in card payment systems
why_relevant: Central-bank research establishing the analytical baseline and Hungarian-specific data on interchange economics; useful as a methodological reference and for historical fee levels pre-cap.

source_name: NAV – online cash register data download service (machine-to-machine OPG log retrieval)
why_relevant: Documents the M2M service (live since Feb 2023) through which a taxpayer can pull their own cash-register log files — receipt-level records that include payment mode. Establishes that transaction-level cash/card data exists and is machine-retrievable, though scoped to the operator's own tills.

source_name: NAV – Tájékoztatás az Azonnali Fizetési Rendszerről (public-sector participant view)
why_relevant: Tax authority guidance on how AFR/secondary account identifiers apply to state collections — evidence of public-sector adoption of the instant scheme, a material volume driver for the operator.

source_name: KSH ICT publications (A vállalkozások és a háztartások IKT-eszközökkel való ellátottsága és használata)
why_relevant: The narrative ICT/e-commerce publications contain the payment-method-of-online-purchase splits (utánvét/cash-on-delivery vs online card vs transfer vs fintech app) that do not appear as standalone STADAT tables.

source_name: KSH – Helyzetkép a kiskereskedelemről (annual retail situation report)
why_relevant: Annual analytical retail report; historically includes store-network, e-commerce and structural detail useful for POS/acceptance-base sizing.

source_name: Bankszövetségi Krónikák (Kovács Levente) - association chronicle PDF
why_relevant: Book-length compilation including 2024 member institutions and extracts from the Association's annual-report management summaries - a rare consolidated historical baseline for the HU banking sector and its digital transition.

entity_name: GIRO Zrt. corporate site + career portal
source_name: GIRO BKR forgalmi statisztika PDF-ek („BKR tranzakciók száma”, /storage/ assets)
why_relevant: The most granular publicly surfaced GIRO series: monthly BKR transaction counts (long history, at least 2000–2022 in observed vintages) split by platform (éjszakai / napközbeni / azonnali elszámolás). This is the raw AFR-uptake and batch-clearing time series.

entity_name: GIRO Zrt. corporate site + career portal
source_name: GIRO BKR Üzletszabályzat (business rules) és mellékletei, incl. HCT Inst üzenetáramlási folyamatleírás
why_relevant: Defines participation rules, cycle structure, cut-offs, message standards (HCT Inst / SEPA-based) and change history of the clearing system — the structural context needed to interpret volume series and to anticipate scheme changes (e.g. AFR 2.0).

source_name: Act CXVI of 2012 on the Financial Transaction Levy (2012. évi CXVI. törvény a pénzügyi tranzakciós illetékről) – Nemzeti Jogszabálytár entry
why_relevant: The core statute defining the levy base and rates per transaction type (transfers, card purchases, cash withdrawal, currency exchange, e-money since 2025-07-20, securities since 2022-08-01); the rate/cap structure is the key to converting levy revenue into implied payment volumes.

source_name: MNB decree setting minimum ATM counts per credit institution (5/2025. (IV.17.) MNB rendelet family, on njt.hu)
why_relevant: Secondary regulation quantifying per-bank ATM operating obligations by card-portfolio band (reported thresholds e.g. min. 169 ATMs for smaller issuers, 1686 for the largest). Directly drives ATM procurement/consolidation volumes.

source_name: Deloitte Digital Hungary – legacy article archive (www2.deloitte.com/hu)
why_relevant: Older Deloitte Digital Hungary articles on digital sales/channel maturity of banks still live on the legacy www2 domain; useful for time series of the Digital Banking Maturity results for Hungary. Note ongoing migration from www2 to www — old links may redirect.

source_name: Big-4 / advisory Hungarian tax alerts on the transaction levy (Deloitte HU, RSM Hungary, Andersen HU)
why_relevant: Advisory alerts summarise levy scope expansions and their operational impact on banks, PSPs and e-money issuers — useful for interpreting how levy changes reshape pricing of card, ATM and transfer transactions.

source_name: EBA/ECB Report on Payment Fraud (2024, 2025 editions)
why_relevant: Joint EBA/ECB harmonised card and credit-transfer fraud statistics by country. Important caveat: the 2025 edition explicitly excludes Hungary because HU data were not available across the full period — a material coverage limitation to record.

source_name: EBA Guidelines on fraud reporting under PSD2 (reporting framework)
why_relevant: Defines what MNB must collect from Hungarian PSPs and forward via EUCLID — tells you which HU fraud/card series will become available, at what granularity, and when.

entity_name: MNB rendelet 19/2025 + methodological guide on mandated ATM installation
source_name: MNB rendelet 19/2025 + methodological guide on mandated ATM installation (bank-by-bank allocation)
why_relevant: The regulation enumerates which bank must install ATMs in which settlements (OTP 428, MBH 195, K&H 117, Erste 104 of 1,039 units), creating a rare bank-level, unit-level ATM pipeline. This is the demand signal that drives HU ATM vendor procurement over 2025-2026.

entity_name: MNB rendelet 19/2025 + methodological guide on mandated ATM installation
source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabálytár / Jogtár – 2025. évi XVIII. törvény az automata bankjegykiadó gépek telepítéséről ("ATM Act")
why_relevant: The legal ATM mandate itself: obliges payment service providers to install ATMs in every settlement on a phased schedule (>1000 inhabitants by end-2025, 500-1000 by end-2026) with MNB fines of HUF 2m-200m. Baseline for compliance-driven ATM deployment tracking.

entity_name: MNB rendelet 19/2025 + methodological guide on mandated ATM installation
source_name: Net Jogtár — 2013. évi CCXXXV. törvény az egyes fizetési szolgáltatókról (Fsztv.)
why_relevant: The statute that creates the payment-institution and e-money-institution categories and the MNB's registration duty. Defines the legal vocabulary used by every MNB register entry and states what must be published — the legal backbone for judging register completeness.

source_name: BIS CPMI Red Book methodology (CPMI d168) and country tables (d172 series)
why_relevant: Defines the Red Book indicator taxonomy (fast payments, non-bank PSPs, contactless) that ECB and MNB definitions are increasingly aligned to; essential for reconciling differing Hungarian figures across aggregators.

source_name: Eurostat Statistics Explained — Hungarian-language article layer (/hu)
why_relevant: Rare case of a supranational aggregator publishing in Hungarian; gives the official HU terminology (e.g. 'infokommunikációs eszközök', 'internetes vásárlás') that maps EU dataset codes to Hungarian search terms for other workstreams.

source_name: Kormany.hu – government communications on the universal ATM / free cash withdrawal obligation
why_relevant: Policy-owner announcements framing the ATM mandate and the HUF 150k free-withdrawal obligation; often the first place deployment targets and deadlines are quantified.

source_name: kormany.hu – government communications on e-pénztárgép / eNyugta rollout
why_relevant: Ministerial/government announcements set the timetable and policy intent for the fiscal-telemetry regime (free NAV ePénztárgép and eNyugta mobile apps), which directly shapes POS/terminal demand and cash-vs-card measurement.

source_name: Mainstream HU business media covering ATM/POS network numbers (Origo, Pénzcentrum, HVG, Portfolio, Forbes.hu)
why_relevant: General business media report ATM-per-settlement rollout programmes and terminal-count milestones, often quoting operators or the ministry before any structured dataset is published. HVG/Forbes also host acquirer brand-content that leaks operational detail (e.g. Global Payments softPOS, Doppio targets).

source_name: Akadémiai szakirodalom – A magyarországi bankközi klíringrendszer működése (PhD disszertáció, ME GTK)
why_relevant: Doctoral research on the operation of the Hungarian interbank clearing system; compiles long historical BKR series and methodology notes that help interpret definitional breaks in operator statistics.

entity_name: Consumer/comparison sites tracking ATM fees and network size
source_name: Consumer/comparison sites tracking ATM fees and network size (Wise HU blog, Biztosdöntés)
why_relevant: These pages track independent-ATM surcharge levels and network descriptions over time; surcharge structure is a leading indicator of IAD economics and of cash-access cost in Hungary, which is not published by the operators themselves.

source_name: Danube Capital — blog: POS terminálok száma Magyarországon
why_relevant: Analyst/advisory firm blog that appears to compile and time-series the Hungarian POS terminal count. Analyst blogs of this kind often present tidier long-run series than the raw MNB tables and reveal the compiler's methodology; valuable both as a data pointer and as a competitor-analysis artefact.

entity_name: E-commerce platform / integrator comparison content on HU PSPs
source_name: E-commerce platform / integrator comparison content on HU PSPs (Shoptet blog, eClick, WeboldalSzeged, Zunapro)
why_relevant: Platform and agency comparisons are the only public source venturing HU PSP market-share estimates (SimplePay ~60-65%, Barion ~20-25%) and up-to-date fee ranges, plus they surface newer entrants (ShoptetPay, Stripe, Paylike) that scheme communications ignore.

source_name: EUR-Lex – Regulation (EU) 2015/751 on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions
why_relevant: The binding interchange caps (0.2%/0.3%) applying directly in Hungary; the numeric anchor against which Hungarian scheme fees, MIF disclosures and merchant-cost analyses must be read. Hungarian language version available via EUR-Lex.

source_name: G7.hu – investigative reporting on ownership of Hungary's cash-handling infrastructure
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly source: documents ownership changes and consolidation among HU CIT/cash-processing firms (G4S Készpénzlogisztikai, TrezEx ex-Brink's/Securitas) and their bank/retail client bases — information not published by the firms themselves.

entity_name: GVH sectoral inquiry report on the card acceptance market
source_name: GVH sectoral inquiry report on the card acceptance market (2019)
why_relevant: Competition-authority sectoral inquiry that compelled data from eight banks, four non-bank card-acceptance providers and two card schemes — effectively a regulator-forced disclosure of the private acquiring/terminal supplier structure that vendors and banks otherwise keep private.

source_name: MagNet Bank – ATM network transition notices (Euronet outsourcing)
why_relevant: Bank-side notices about handing ATM estates to Euronet reveal outsourcing deals and effective network sizes ('over 500 Euronet ATMs available to customers') that neither party announces as a headline statistic — an indirect but datable indicator of ATM-estate consolidation in Hungary.

source_name: The Paypers — annual payments & fintech events calendar
why_relevant: Curated international event calendar; identifies the regional (CEE/EU) events where Hungarian banks, GIRO and MNB staff speak and where HU-relevant scheme roadmaps (IPR, ISO 20022, wallets) are presented.
